# /data — Synthetic Datasets & Splits

## What lives here

Three generated datasets and a split utility, all produced by deterministic Python scripts (with LLM-assisted generation for Hinglish transcript text only). Every distribution parameter below is calibrated against published Indian payment system data — see `/references/sources.md` for the full citation trail.

---

## Dataset A: Failed Recurring Payment Records

**File:** `failed_payments.json`
**Size:** 500 records
**Generated by:** `generate_payments.py`

### Schema

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `payment_id` | string | Unique ID (e.g., `PAY_00001`) |
| `customer_id` | string | Non-unique — some customers have multiple failed payments |
| `mandate_id` | string | Links to a recurring mandate; shared across payments for same customer |
| `amount` | float | ₹ amount. Range depends on `payment_category` |
| `payment_category` | enum | `subscription`, `emi`, `sip`, `insurance`, `cc_bill` |
| `payment_method` | enum | `upi_autopay`, `enach`, `card_auto_debit` |
| `bank_name` | string | Real Indian bank names, weighted by actual UPI transaction volume share |
| `bin` | string | 6-digit BIN, consistent with `bank_name` |
| `failure_timestamp` | datetime | Spread across 30 simulated days with deliberate clustering patterns |
| `failure_reason_code` | string | What the system reports — uses real NPCI NACH codes where applicable (see code mapping below) |
| `customer_prior_success_count` | int | Historical successful payments |
| `customer_prior_failure_count` | int | Historical failed payments |
| `mandate_expiry_date` | date | Actual mandate expiry. For `mandate_revoked`: AFTER failure (mandate was still valid when customer cancelled) |
| `amount_above_afa_threshold` | bool | Whether amount exceeds the AFA threshold for this payment's category (₹15,000 for subscription/emi; ₹1,00,000 for sip/insurance/cc_bill per RBI e-mandate framework 2026) |
| `pre_debit_notification_sent` | bool | Whether the mandatory 24h pre-debit notification was sent before the debit attempt |
| `ground_truth_cause` | enum | **Evaluation only — diagnosis layer must NEVER read this.** One of: `bank_outage`, `insufficient_funds`, `mandate_expired`, `mandate_revoked`, `card_expired`, `afa_stuck`, `ambiguous` |

### Failure reason code mapping (NPCI NACH codes)

Based on NPCI circular NPCI/2024-25/NACH/006 and Decentro API docs:

| Code | NPCI meaning | Maps from ground_truth_cause |
|---|---|---|
| `04` | Balance Insufficient | `insufficient_funds` |
| `59` | Network Failure (CBS) | `bank_outage` (also used in ambiguous) |
| `14` | Mandate expired | `mandate_expired` |
| `61` | Mandate Cancelled | `mandate_revoked` |
| `card_expired` | Card network code (no NACH equivalent) | `card_expired` |
| `afa_pending` | UPI-specific (no NACH equivalent) | `afa_stuck` |
| `timeout` | Generic timeout — ambiguous between bank/network/AFA | `bank_outage`, `afa_stuck`, `ambiguous` |
| `unknown` | Unmapped/unclassified | `bank_outage`, `afa_stuck`, `ambiguous` |

### Payment categories and AFA thresholds

Per RBI Digital Payments E-Mandate Framework 2026:

| Category | Amount range | AFA threshold | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| `subscription` | ₹99–₹999 | ₹15,000 | OTT, SaaS, news — always below threshold |
| `emi` | ₹2,000–₹50,000 | ₹15,000 | Phone, appliance, personal loan EMIs — frequently above threshold |
| `sip` | ₹500–₹25,000 | ₹1,00,000 | Mutual fund SIPs — elevated threshold per RBI Dec 2023 circular |
| `insurance` | ₹1,000–₹50,000 | ₹1,00,000 | Insurance premiums — elevated threshold |
| `cc_bill` | ₹500–₹80,000 | ₹1,00,000 | Credit card bill payments — elevated threshold |

### Cause distribution (calibrated against published data)

| Cause | Approx % | Calibration source |
|---|---|---|
| `insufficient_funds` | ~30% | Most common single cause; 20M UPI AutoPay revocations/month due to low balance (Business Standard Sep 2025) |
| `bank_outage` | ~20% | NPCI bank downtime data; scoped to recurring-payment-specific share |
| `mandate_expired` | ~10% | Mandate lifecycle — eNACH/UPI Autopay specific |
| `mandate_revoked` | ~5% | 20M mandates revoked/month (Business Standard); customer actively cancelled |
| `card_expired` | ~12% | Credit card issuance churn (113M cards, ~8% YoY per Worldline Q3 2025) |
| `afa_stuck` | ~13% | RBI AFA threshold blocks without customer action |
| `ambiguous` | ~10% | Conflicting signals, no clean single cause |

### Bank distribution (weighted by real transaction volume)

Based on NPCI's published remitter-bank UPI volumes:

| Bank | Approx weight | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| SBI | ~25% | Highest volume; ~30% AutoPay approval rate (Business Standard); 5 incidents, 5h39m downtime |
| HDFC | ~15% | Second-highest volume, >99.9% availability |
| Bank of Baroda | ~10% | Third-highest volume, 94.87% approval rate |
| ICICI | ~8% | Fourth by volume, 95.14% approval |
| Axis | ~7% | Fifth by volume, highest approval rate among top 5 (96.54%) |
| PNB | ~6% | 4 downtime incidents, 7h57m total — second-worst downtime record |
| Union Bank | ~5% | 94.84% approval, 5.09% BD |
| Kotak | ~5% | 95.04% approval |
| Bank of India | ~4% | 96.74% approval |
| Canara, IDBI, others | ~15% combined | Fills out the tail |

### Timestamp clustering patterns

Based on the peak failure periods identified in VyaparGateway and NPCI data:
- **Month-end cluster (days 27–31):** elevated failure rate, especially `insufficient_funds` (EMI debits + salary timing)
- **Bank-outage bursts:** 12–18 failures sharing a BIN within a 2-hour window, concentrated on SBI, PNB, and Bank of Baroda
- **Late-night cluster (10PM–midnight):** batch processing window, elevated `timeout` and `59`
- **Post-holiday spike:** first business day after a weekend/holiday

### Deliberate edge cases (25+ injected)

- Records with missing or malformed BIN
- Customer with 0 prior history (brand new)
- Mandate expiry date only 1 day before failure timestamp
- Payment that looks like bank_outage by BIN clustering but is actually `insufficient_funds` (false-positive case)
- Duplicate customer entries with different causes across payments
- Amount exactly at ₹15,000 AFA threshold (emi category)
- `59` (Network Failure) reason code on a record whose ground truth is actually `bank_outage` (reason code ≠ root cause)
- `timeout` reason code on an `afa_stuck` case (customer never completed AFA, system sees timeout)
- `mandate_revoked` records where pre-debit notification was sent (customer saw it and then cancelled — deliberate signal)

## Dataset B: Historical Retry Outcomes

**File:** `retry_outcomes.json`
**Size:** 1,200 records
**Generated by:** `generate_retry_outcomes.py`

### Schema

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `retry_id` | string | Unique |
| `original_cause` | enum | Same cause labels as Dataset A (includes `mandate_revoked`) |
| `retry_attempt_number` | int | 1, 2, or 3 |
| `time_of_day` | int | Hour (0–23) |
| `day_of_week` | int | 0–6 |
| `days_since_failure` | int | How many days after the original failure this retry was attempted |
| `days_since_estimated_payday` | int | -15 to +15 |
| `amount` | float | ₹ amount |
| `action_type` | enum | `auto_retry`, `sms_then_retry`, `call_then_retry` |
| `action_cost` | float | ₹0 / ₹2 / ₹15 respectively |
| `pre_debit_notification_sent` | bool | Whether the pre-debit notification was sent before this retry |
| `outcome` | enum | `success` or `failure` |
| `amount_recovered` | float | = `amount` if success, 0 if failure |

### Embedded patterns (what the bandit should learn)

These are the signals deliberately baked into the data. Documented here so (a) I can verify the bandit actually recovers them, and (b) to be transparent that the bandit uplift number reflects recovery of known patterns, not discovery of unknown ones.

- `insufficient_funds` retries succeed at higher rates 0–3 days after estimated payday (customer has been paid)
- `bank_outage` retries succeed at higher rates when retried within 6–12 hours (outage has resolved)
- `card_expired`, `mandate_expired`, and `mandate_revoked` retries almost never succeed — these need a different action entirely
- 3rd retry attempts have lower success rates than 1st attempts across all causes (diminishing returns)
- `sms_then_retry` has modestly higher success than `auto_retry` for `insufficient_funds` (customer sees SMS and tops up)
- `call_then_retry` has highest success rate but also highest cost (₹15) — the net-₹ reward function should learn when it's worth the cost
- `pre_debit_notification_sent=False` + `insufficient_funds` → slightly higher retry recovery (customer didn't know debit was coming; just notifying them helps)

## Dataset C: Train/Test Splits

**Generated by:** `split_data.py`

Two split strategies, both applied to Dataset A:

1. **Stratified split (80/20)** — every `ground_truth_cause` label appears proportionally in both train and test
2. **Time-based split** — earlier 80% by `failure_timestamp` = train, later 20% = test

The script prints a summary of cause distribution in each split for manual verification. Diagnosis rules are tuned on the train split only; accuracy is reported on the test split, once, without re-tuning.

---

## Important: what `ground_truth_cause` is and isn't

This column exists ONLY for evaluation. The diagnosis layer receives every other column but never sees `ground_truth_cause`. If at any point the diagnosis code reads this column, the accuracy number is meaningless — it's the equivalent of looking at the answer key during a test.

The `failure_reason_code` column (which the diagnosis layer DOES see) deliberately does not always match `ground_truth_cause`. This is realistic: a `59` (Network Failure CBS) can mask a bank-wide outage, a `timeout` can be network-side or bank-side or AFA-related, and `unknown` means the system genuinely doesn't know. The diagnosis layer's job is to use contextual signals (BIN clustering, mandate dates, AFA threshold + category, notification status, prior history) to infer the real cause despite noisy/ambiguous reason codes.

## Generated Output (actual distributions from seed=42/7)

### Dataset A: Failed Payments (500 records)

| ground_truth_cause | Count | % |
|---|---|---|
| insufficient_funds | 150 | 30.0% |
| bank_outage | 100 | 20.0% |
| afa_stuck | 65 | 13.0% |
| card_expired | 60 | 12.0% |
| mandate_expired | 50 | 10.0% |
| ambiguous | 50 | 10.0% |
| mandate_revoked | 25 | 5.0% |

| payment_category | Count | % |
|---|---|---|
| emi | 197 | 39.4% |
| subscription | 121 | 24.2% |
| sip | 85 | 17.0% |
| insurance | 56 | 11.2% |
| cc_bill | 41 | 8.2% |

Pre-debit notification sent: 80.8%. Not sent: 19.2%.

AFA threshold (category-aware): 192 records (38.4%) above their category's threshold. EMIs dominate (163/197 above ₹15K), while subscriptions (0/121) and cc_bills (0/41) are never above their respective thresholds.

Bank outage clustering: 7 incidents across 5 banks (SBI ×2, PNB ×2, Bank of Baroda ×1, Bank of India ×1, ICICI ×1), each 12–18 records within 2-hour windows.

Mandate revoked: 25 records, all with `mandate_expiry_date` after `failure_timestamp` (mandate was still valid when cancelled). 72% had pre-debit notification sent.

### Dataset B: Retry Outcomes (1,200 records)

Pattern verification (success rates):

| Pattern | Rate | Control | Signal strength |
|---|---|---|---|
| insufficient_funds near payday (0–3 days) | 51.0% | 33.8% (far) | +17.2pp |
| bank_outage well-timed (≤1d, 6–18h) | 61.1% | 41.2% (poor) | +19.9pp |
| card/mandate expired+revoked | 8.0% | — | Near zero |
| Attempt 1 vs Attempt 3 | 31.2% | 19.3% | −11.9pp |
| insuf_funds sms vs auto | 36.2% | 25.2% | +11.0pp |
| insuf_funds notif sent vs not sent | 35.2% | 39.5% | +4.3pp (no-notif higher) |

Pre-debit notification: 76.3% sent, 23.7% not sent.

### Dataset C: Train/Test Splits

**Stratified (80/20):** proportions preserved across all 7 cause categories.

**Temporal:** train covers Jan 1–27, test covers Jan 27–30. Temporal test is dominated by insufficient_funds (63%) due to month-end clustering — this is realistic and by design.
